clue.text: Novel about to record artist's weight

indicators.note: the novel's title is wrapped around the other pieces, as if circling them

parts.note: Kim is Rudyard Kipling's novel
a log is a written record
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone wants to note down a painter's heaviness, with a novel close by.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilogram is a metric unit of mass, an everyday measure of weight.

clue.text: Secured enthusiast for scene of folly

parts.note: to have got something is to have secured it
a ham is an amateur radio enthusiast

explanation.surface: A fan was obtained for the setting of a foolish act.
explanation.walkthrough: Gotham, a Nottinghamshire village, was proverbial for its 'wise men', whose antics were famously foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: The English village of the 'Wise Men' tales is a byword for folly and simple-minded villagers.

clue.text: Mix fuel essence, losing money in Japan

parts.note: coal is a fuel

indicators.note: the word essence drops some letters, as if they were lost from it

parts.note: taken as written
the sen is a small Japanese coin

explanation.surface: Blend fuel extract while dropping yen in Tokyo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes SEN out of ESSENCE, leaving ESCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coalesce is to merge or come together, much as things combine when mixed.

clue.text: Sage raised cry of woe about shrinking violet

indicators.note: the reversed cry goes around the shortened flower
in a down clue the word is lifted, so it reads from bottom upward

parts.note: alas is a cry of grief

indicators.note: the word violet is cut down to its opening letters, as if it shrank

explanation.surface: A herb is lifted up with a lament about a shy, retiring person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrinking violet' looks like a shy person, but it asks for the flower's name cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvia is the botanical genus that includes culinary sage, so it is a plant name for the herb.

clue.text: Stand to take drugs — take too many?

parts.note: to trip is to be on hallucinogenic drugs
OD stands for overdose, taking too much of a drug

explanation.surface: A support for drug use, and then excess.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged support, a stand for a camera or telescope.

clue.text: Interfere with packer

definitions.meaning: to meddle or fiddle with something
a tool or person that tamps or packs material down

explanation.definitionFit: To tamper is to meddle; and a tamper is also a tool for ramming earth or tobacco down.

clue.text: Young animal entertaining the graduate element

indicators.note: the foal hosts the degree inside it, as a host entertains a guest

parts.note: a colt is a young horse
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A foal amuses a fresh university leaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobalt is a metallic chemical element, number 27 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Cancer, say, left over one hundred

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is turned over, read from the bottom up

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A remark about the disease, with something remaining beyond a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns PORT into TROP. 'Cancer' looks like the disease but is the Tropic of Cancer; 'say' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tropic of Cancer is one of the two tropics, the line of latitude north of the equator.

clue.text: Device torn apart in explanatory text

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit inside the text word

parts.note: a caption is the text explaining a picture

indicators.note: the letters of torn are pulled apart and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gadget is ripped up inside a description beneath a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraption is a strange or improvised machine, a gadget or device.

clue.text: Pet's low note breaks silence

indicators.note: the pieces burst into the middle of the hush word

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
to low is to moo, as cattle do
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A dog's bark breaks the quiet of a household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' puts MOO and C inside SH. The 's after Pet stands for 'is'. 'low' is a verb, the sound cows make.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet in the amorous sense is to kiss and cuddle, which is exactly what smooching means.

clue.text: Having no memory of deceased cat swallowing 4

parts.note: ob, for obiit, marks someone who died

indicators.note: the cat takes the numeral inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: a lion is a big cat
IV is 4 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone forgets a dead cat that swallowed something.
explanation.walkthrough: '4' looks like a cross-reference to 4-down but is just the number, IV in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivion is the condition of forgetting entirely, a state of having no memory of something.

clue.text: Raise rump

definitions.meaning: to bring up children or animals

explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to bring up young; the rear is also the hindquarters or bottom.

clue.text: Turning to a sea mist for supplier of 22s

indicators.note: the letters are turned around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Changing into a fog over the water, as a poet supplied texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is 22-across, LIBRETTO: Pietro Metastasio was the 18th-century Italian poet who wrote libretti for many operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Metastasio was the most prolific librettist of his age, so he supplied the texts for operas.

clue.text: John returned in atmosphere of uncertainty

indicators.note: the reversed word goes inside the atmosphere word

parts.note: ambience is the mood or atmosphere of a place

indicators.note: the word is sent back, read right to left

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, a lav

explanation.surface: A man named John came back into a mood of doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: John is not a man but slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambivalence is having mixed feelings, a state of uncertainty about which way to go.

clue.text: Temptation? No, ta! Drunk and unable to respond

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, and removed from the pool

explanation.surface: Turning down an offer of a drink, a man who is past responding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No, ta!' says to take TA out of TEMPTATION; 'Drunk' scrambles the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Impotent means powerless, especially sexually unable to respond.

clue.text: Fool wearing garment gains energy from muse

indicators.note: gains means the letter is added at the end
the fool is inside the coat, as if wearing it

parts.note: a coat is a garment
git is British slang for a stupid person
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A clown in a costume draws inspiration from a goddess of the arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muse' looks like a goddess of the arts but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To cogitate is to think deeply, to ponder or muse on something.

clue.text: Gregarious agents in the sun

indicators.note: the agency sits inside the sun word

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, staffed by agents

explanation.surface: Friendly spies relaxing in the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: A social person enjoys company, just as a gregarious one does.

clue.text: Defective gun's all right inside

indicators.note: the okay goes inside the gun

parts.note: the Bren is a British light machine gun
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A faulty weapon is nonetheless sound inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts OK inside BREN. The 's after gun stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something broken is faulty or not working, so it is defective.

clue.text: Stolen drug found among churches' jumble

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods

indicators.note: the drug is placed between the two church abbreviations

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church, and two churches give CH twice
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Stolen narcotics discovered amid church clutter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found among' puts POT between the two CHs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotchpotch is a confused mixture, a jumble of odds and ends.

clue.text: Copper to upbraid churchman

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate is an old word for to scold

explanation.surface: A policeman about to tell off a priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A curate is an assistant to a parish priest, a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Leader of Levites in the Pentateuch picked up Jezebel

indicators.note: in a down clue picked up means read from the bottom upward
the single letter goes inside the scripture word

parts.note: the Torah is the five books of Moses, the Pentateuch

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A biblical tale about Levites and the wicked queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L into TORAH as TOLRAH; 'picked up' turns that into HARLOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Jezebel, the wicked biblical queen, became a byword for a shameless woman or harlot.

clue.text: Clothes to boast about

indicators.note: about here means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: to brag is to boast

explanation.surface: Garments worth showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Garb means clothing, particularly a distinctive style of dress.

clue.text: "Roving Rob" — title of book

indicators.note: roving means wandering, so the letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wandering rogue named Rob gives his name to a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'book' is the opera sense: the words of an opera are its book.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the text of an opera or musical, known in theatre as its book.

clue.text: Get back! Sit! Again!

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to sit an exam is to take it

explanation.surface: Barked commands to a dog: come back, sit, do it again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like dog training; the pieces come in answer order, RE first.
explanation.definitionFit: To retake something is to recapture it, getting back what was lost.

clue.text: Fired indiscriminately at catalogue

parts.note: lit means set on fire
any, as in any one at all, means chosen without discrimination

explanation.surface: Someone shot wildly at a target.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a long list or recital, a tedious catalogue of complaints, say.

clue.text: Wanderers keep escaping!

parts.note: to bolt is to run off or escape
on means continuing, as in keep going or carry on

explanation.surface: A cry about prisoners who won't stop breaking out.
explanation.walkthrough: Bolton Wanderers is an English football club; 'Wanderers' looks like plain drifters.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club Bolton Wanderers is commonly called just Bolton, so its nickname names the town.
